Hi @Rémy Degenne, how are you? Using the opportunity to look into the project and see if I can add any contribution.

I have a lean proof ready for two martingale identities of IsFilteredPreBrownian for square and Wald exponential martingale properties:

  • t↦Xt2−tt \mapsto X_t^2 - tt↦Xt2​−t is a martingale w.r.t. F\mathcal{F}F
  • t↦exp⁡(αXt−α2t/2)t \mapsto \exp(\alpha X_t - \alpha^2 t / 2)t↦exp(αXt​−α2t/2) is a martingale w.r.t. F\mathcal{F}F, for every α∈R\alpha \in \mathbb{R}α∈R

what I thought is a possible step after IsPreBrownian.isMartingale, with a new file BrownianMotion/Gaussian/Martingale.lean with no new external deps.

It uses existing mathlib gaussianReal api + the project's IsFilteredPreBrownian.indep / hasLaw_sub / hasLaw_eval.

I wanted to check if this is an issue worth opening. I can claim and pr later if it makes sense. Happy to discuss the approach first.

thanks!

cc @Etienne Marion

Hi Raphael, glad to hear you're interested in contributing to the project! I think it would help to see your code for saying if this is useful for the project or not. Do you keep it somewhere in a public repository that you could link to?

You might want to take a look at the PDF here #Brownian motion > Status of the project @ 💬 which explains the approach we're taking for formalising stochastic integrals and (if you haven't already) the contributing guidelines. There are many ways to contribute, a good way to start is usually to claim one of the open tasks. It's even possible to help without directly writing Lean code by working on the blueprint, maybe this could also be interesting for you.

hi Jonas, many thanks!

Here is the code on the two martingale identities:
https://github.com/raphaelrrcoelho/formal-mathfin/blob/main/upstream/brownian-motion/Martingale.lean

Thanks for the PDF ref there. I took a look and I realized that i have another piece of code that could be tangential to the Itô isometry milestone from a BM angle. It's the Wiener integral L² isometry against ´IsPreBrownian´ in https://github.com/raphaelrrcoelho/formal-mathfin/blob/main/MathFin/Foundations/WienerIntegralL2.lean. It would be nice if you could also take a look to see if it's of interest for the project.

I will dive into the open tasks and the blueprint to familiarize myself better with how to get more involved. :-)

These are purely AI generated, while the repo does not typically do AI PRs. Even if suitable, there would a very non-trivial effort of cleaning it up, which will need some manual intervention and human (your) understanding in the process.

May I ask why you want to put this into the repo specifically? AI code can usually "get the job done" nowadays, and AI use is typically about being pragmatic and result oriented, whereas human dominated lean repos often seek insight and human understanding of the most hollistic way to formalise any said maths.

Hey Yan.

I have engaged solving all the proofs of theorems in my grad course in stochastic processes. The course covers from discrete markov chain to itô calculus with applications (mostly in finance).

After doing that, I was curious to see if I could port then to Lean/Isabelle/Sympy as an exercise to learn how the formal proofs work in an automated fashion. I thought that I would be able to migrate all of them to Lean, for instance, but didnt realize that many complex building blocks are still being developed in projects like this one.

When my port of these proofs in the course material couldnt advance because of the absence this or that route, that's when I started getting curious if any of these would be useful for the mathlib main repo.
